review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp-tagged declarations for loops, competing rules and unwanted expansion. They are the coe, mem, toAddSubmonoid, self and restrictScalars_restrictScalars lemmas; the le, lt, inj, bot, top, eq_bot_iff and eq_top_iff lemmas; the sInf, sSup, iInf, iSup, inf and sup lemmas; the disjoint, codisjoint and isCompl iff lemmas; and the @[simps] output for the embedding and equiv. All of them rewrite `restrictScalars S x` outward or reduce to a smaller form, so I saw no credible cycle. The eq_bot_iff and eq_top_iff lemmas are not subsumed by `restrictScalars_inj` plus `restrictScalars_bot` and `restrictScalars_top`, because those two rewrite `restrictScalars S ⊥` to `⊥` and not the reverse. The image form in `restrictScalars_sSup` and `restrictScalars_sInf` is not expanded further, because `sSup_image` and `sInf_image` are not simp in Mathlib/Order/CompleteLattice/Basic.lean. I also checked `toIntSubmodule_toAddSubgroup` (line 175) against `AddSubgroup.toIntSubmodule_toAddSubgroup` (simp) and `Submodule.toAddSubgroup_toIntSubmodule` (not simp) in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Lattice.lean. For `R = ℤ` the target lemma plus `restrictScalars_self` should in principle cover the non-simp one, but I could not confirm that the `SMul ℤ ℤ` instances unify, so I did not report it. No lemma rewrites `(N.restrictScalars ℤ).toAddSubgroup`, but I found no uses that need one. Without running Lean I could not test any simp behavior, and I found nothing concrete enough to recommend.
